gold_rationale: An α-synuclein aggregation modulator is mechanistically aligned with PD Lewy pathology and the candidate has CNS penetration plus preclinical pathology effects. But the mechanism is non-classical: target engagement is hard to define and there is no validated clinical biomarker, and anti-aggregation small molecules have a poor preclinical-to-clinical track record. Progression should be a Conditional Go contingent on developing/validating a target-engagement or pathology biomarker (PET ligand, CSF/seed-amplification readout), confirming CNS exposure, and clearing standard ADMET/safety. A No-Go is defensible if the team cannot define measurable target engagement. The central issue is the biomarker/target-engagement gap, not potency; mechanistic plausibility is not proven disease modification.
red_flags: claims proven disease modification from preclinical pathology effects
ignores the target-engagement / biomarker measurement problem
ignores the poor clinical track record of anti-aggregation molecules
treats in vitro aggregation reduction as proof of clinical efficacy
